# Zendesk app source

This package is an isolated source contribution for the Zendesk connector feed. `index.ts` uses
the public `example` placeholder. The feed builder reads the trusted tenant runtime setting
`EXECUTOR_ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN` and calls `createZendeskApp` while building that tenant's source. Tool
input never selects a host. The provider allows credential requests to exactly
`<subdomain>.zendesk.com`.

The app uses per-user OAuth accounts and exposes `currentUser`, `listTickets`, `getTicket`, and
`createTicket`. Ticket creation always needs user approval. Account health checks `GET
/api/v2/users/me.json` and uses that user's `id` and `name` as the connection identity.

## Zendesk local OAuth client

Create a local OAuth client in the same Zendesk tenant under **Admin Center → Apps and integrations
→ APIs → OAuth clients**. Choose **Confidential**. Register the exact redirect URI shown by the
Executor OAuth connection flow, `https://app.signalbox.run/api/oauth/callback`. Name the client
`Signalbox`. Set its allowed scopes to:

```text
tickets:read tickets:write users:read
```

The source requests those same scopes. `users:read` covers account health's current-user lookup.
Do not configure a global shared Zendesk account for this app. The hosted client secrets are
`EXECUTOR_OAUTH_ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID` and `EXECUTOR_OAUTH_ZENDESK_CLIENT_SECRET`; they are consumed by
the host's native OAuth configuration and never appear in app source.

The native app OAuth runtime uses PKCE S256. Current Zendesk docs specify the authorization URL as
`https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com/oauth/authorizations/new` and the token URL as
`https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens`. They require JSON token requests with
`client_secret_post`. A refresh request includes `grant_type=refresh_token`, `refresh_token`,
`client_id`, and `client_secret`; Zendesk rotates both tokens, so the new pair must replace the old
pair. The current Zendesk Developer refresh example omits `scope`, `expires_in`, and
`refresh_token_expires_in`. The API accepts those optional settings, but token lifetimes default to
30 minutes and 30 days. The native SDK omits scope on ordinary native refresh grants by design,
which matches Zendesk's four-field refresh example and RFC 6749 section 6. The SDK sends JSON for
sign-in and renewal and persists both rotated tokens, so no Zendesk-specific refresh transport is
needed.

Sources: [Zendesk OAuth setup](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210-Using-OAuth-authentication-with-your-application), [grant type token API](https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/grant_type_tokens/), [Zendesk refresh-token guide](https://developer.zendesk.com/documentation/authentication/refresh-token/).

Zendesk documents `/oauth/authorizations/new`; this source follows that endpoint even though the
task brief shortened it to `/oauth/authorizations`.

## Local checks

The package manifest pins published `apps@0.0.1-beta.100`, matching the host runtime supported by
the current official app sources. The separate prepared `apps@0.0.1-beta.104-basalt.1` snapshot was
used only as the local native proof harness. Run the source typecheck against the published package,
then run the mocked public-host scenarios:

```sh
bun run typecheck
bun run test
```

The tests run the public app host adapter with mocked HTTP. They do not contact Zendesk or need
credentials.
